core_obligations: Translate the equivalence (proof lines 7148-7152): a morphism of quotients is the same as a morphism of groupoids in functors over the category, so it is given by morphisms phi on U and psi on R.

Show phi is an isomorphism (proof lines 7152-7166): the displayed square comparing the actions of the derivations of the residue field on TU and on the tangent space of the quotient commutes; since the differential of the equivalence is bijective, minimality of the groupoid forces the differential of phi to be injective, hence bijective by dimension reasons, and therefore phi is an isomorphism by the criterion for morphisms of prorepresentable functors.

Conclude for psi (proof lines 7166-7174): the same argument applied to the exact sequence computing the infinitesimal automorphisms of the quotient proves that psi is an isomorphism as well; alternatively this follows formally from the identity expressing R as a fibre product of U with itself over the quotient together with the fact that phi is an isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Translate the self-equivalence into morphisms of the groupoid in functors.
Use the commuting square of tangent spaces and minimality to make the differential of phi bijective.
Apply the surjectivity criterion, and handle psi either by the exact sequence or by the fibre product description.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a self-equivalence of the quotient of a minimal smooth prorepresentable groupoid in functors on the category of Artinian algebras is an isomorphism (statement lines 7140-7146). The proof (proof lines 7148-7177) translates the equivalence into a pair of morphisms, uses the commuting square of tangent spaces and minimality to make the first one an isomorphism, and handles the second either through the exact sequence of infinitesimal automorphisms or through the fibre product description. H2: a diagram chase with two routes for the second half, written out in full.
